shorts.title: Ravens Fake-Hide Their Food to Fool Thieves 🐦‍⬛
shorts.description:
Ravens fake hiding their food. On purpose. Ravens have been seen sliding down snowbanks, apparently just for fun.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Common raven: Irina Mitine (CC BY), CC0, Chris Quirin (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: Has a bird ever outsmarted you? 👇

shorts.title: This Newt Stabs With Its Own Ribs 🦴
shorts.description:
This newt stabs with its own ribs. Iberian ribbed newts have been studied in space on at least six missions, starting in 1985.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: This Bug Wears a Gear and Drinks Its Prey ⚙️
shorts.description:
This bug wears a gear on its back. The wheel only appears after the final molt into an adult.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: Why Do Scorpions Glow Under a Blacklight? 🦂
shorts.description:
Scorpions glow under a blacklight. About 25 of the 2,500+ scorpion species have venom that can kill a person; some species can go a year without eating.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Striped bark scorpion: Alan Rockefeller (CC BY), dhasdf (CC BY), Laura Clark (CC BY), Nathan May (CC BY), Audrey Witherington (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: What did you guess the glow was for? 👇

shorts.title: Why This Beetle Buries Dead Mice 🪦
shorts.description:
This beetle steals dead mice. The American burying beetle once lived in 35 US states; today it is found in about 9.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Burying beetle: Darren Obbard (CC BY), CC0, Michael Warner (CC BY), Declan McCabe (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0

shorts.title: The Luna Moth's One Huge Problem 🌙
shorts.description:
Luna moths have one huge problem. Luna moth caterpillars click as a warning and can throw up on attackers.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths
